result.title: When Perception Collides with Priors: Diagnosing Modal Polarization in Video Understanding Models
result.comment: 18 pages (main paper with appendix), 11 figures, 8 tables
result.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong video comprehension, largely benefiting from extensive training on realistic video data. However, when video perception severely conflicts with internal priors or common sense, we identify a critical failure pattern termed Modal Polarization, where models fail to integrate modalities and instead bifurcate into two distinct extremes: Cognitive Inertia, where models rigidly adhere to priors despite contradictory visual evidence, and Perceptual Inertia, where they blindly trust video perception while ignoring logical inconsistencies. To investigate this, we introduce TheaterBench, a benchmark designed to expose Modal Polarization using counter-intuitive scenarios that violate physical laws or common sense - situations rarely encountered in standard training distributions. Extensive experiments reveal that current state-of-the-art (SOTA) models exhibit severe Modal Polarization, and many de-hallucination methods merely rebalance the trade-off between Perceptual and Cognitive Inertia rather than fundamentally resolving the conflict. This work serves as a foundational step for evaluating and enhancing the perceptual-cognitive equilibrium of future video understanding models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文识别视频理解 MLLM 在视觉证据与内部先验冲突时出现的「模态极化」失败模式，即认知惯性（固守先验）与知觉惯性（盲信画面），并构建 TheaterBench 反常识基准加以诊断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于模型是否真正采纳视觉证据、先验如何压过感知的失败分析，与 LVR 中视觉信息保留、证据筛选及答案使用问题直接相关；可核查其冲突场景是否也能解释 latent 推理中的视觉旁路与信息坍缩。
